land.text: the Kingdom of Etruria, 'created from the Grand Duchy of Tuscany' and 'a large part of modern Tuscany'

predecessors.note: 'The Grand Duchy was then dissolved, and replaced by the Kingdom of Etruria' (Tuscany page; infobox 21 March 1801). Ferdinand III, the Grand Duke, 'became Elector of Salzburg instead'. Cliopatria's Grand Duchy row carries only a 1,032 km2 fragment for 1800-1802.

land.text: the whole kingdom: 'In 1807, Napoleon dissolved the kingdom and integrated it into France'

successors.note: Formally annexed to France on 30 May 1808 (Tuscany page); administered by an Extraordinary Giunta and divided into the departments of Arno, Méditerranée and Ombrone; from March 1809 a General Government under Elisa Bonaparte as Grand Duchess of Tuscany (see grand-duchy-of-tuscany).

rulers.name: Charles Louis (infobox: Louis II)
rulers.note: An infant; the infobox lists 'Louis II' for 1803-1807 but the body text names the successor Charles Louis, a conflict the page leaves open.

rulers.name: Maria Luisa of Spain
rulers.title: Regent
rulers.note: Mother of the infant king; the Tuscany page says she learned on 23 November 1807 that she must leave, and left on 10 December 1807. [Reviewer eu-20-c, 2026-10-31: source added: the infobox lists '1803–1807: Maria Luisa'.]

correction.text: unchanged shape: the kingdom's land is the Cliopatria 1803 shape, which the pages do not contradict ('created from the Grand Duchy of Tuscany', 'a large part of modern Tuscany'); the change is only in the years, 1801-1802

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Etruria row begins in 1803 but the kingdom was established on 21 March 1801 (Treaty of Aranjuez). Cliopatria's Grand Duchy of Tuscany shapes for 1800-1802 are a 1,032 km2 fragment and do not cover the kingdom's land.

23,128 km2 against the infobox 15,200 km2 (5,850 sq mi, dated 1808): ratio 1.52, inside the factor of two. The shape has 87 cells, about as many as the modern region of Tuscany (86); the page says only 'a large part of modern Tuscany' and does not discuss Lucca, Massa-Carrara, Elba, Piombino or the Presidi, so the 1.5 excess may be those lands and a gap-filler should check them against a page.

correction.text: unchanged shape: the Cliopatria 1806 shape, held through 1807 because the kingdom lasted until 10 December 1807

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria ends the row in 1806; the infobox gives 'Disestablished: December 10, 1807' and the body 'In 1807, Napoleon dissolved the kingdom'. The shape is right; only its years are short by one (see the new keyframe for 1807).

correction.text: unchanged shape: the Cliopatria 1806 shape, extended to the kingdom's last year

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the year Cliopatria omits. The kingdom still held its land until the regent left on 10 December 1807; formal annexation to France followed on 30 May 1808 (Tuscany page).

region.text: the Kingdom of Etruria, 'created from the Grand Duchy of Tuscany' and 'a large part of modern Tuscany'

ledger.note: 21 March 1801: the Treaty of Aranjuez creates the Kingdom of Etruria. 'The kingdom was created by the Treaty of Aranjuez, signed at Aranjuez, Spain on 21 March 1801' (infobox 'Established: March 21, 1801'); Ferdinand of Parma 'had to cede his duchy to France, and his son Louis I was granted the Kingdom of Etruria' from the Grand Duchy of Tuscany. The page draws no boundary: the land is the Cliopatria shape.

10 December 1807: Etruria is taken into France. 'In 1807, Napoleon dissolved the kingdom and integrated it into France' (infobox 'Disestablished: December 10, 1807'); the Tuscany page: by the Treaty of Fontainebleau of 27 October 1807 Etruria 'was to be annexed by France', the regent learned on 23 November she must leave and left on 10 December, and 'On 30 May 1808, Etruria was formally annexed to France'.

1807: the Kingdom of Etruria ends. Infobox 'Disestablished: December 10, 1807'; the land passes to France (formal annexation 30 May 1808) and from 1809 to the General Government of Tuscany under Elisa Bonaparte (Tuscany page).

certainty.note: No page opened gives boundary lines for the kingdom; the shape is Cliopatria's, and the Lucca, Massa-Carrara, Elba, Piombino and Presidi edges are unchecked.

notes: Cliopatria's two shapes (1803-1805, 1806) are the right land but Cliopatria begins two years late (the kingdom was established 21 March 1801) and ends one year early (disestablished 10 December 1807); new keyframes 1801 and 1807 repeat the 1803 and 1806 shapes. The shape is 87 cells, as large as the modern region of Tuscany, while the infobox gives 15,200 km2 (1808); the pages opened say nothing on Lucca, Massa-Carrara, Elba, Piombino or the Stato dei Presidi, which a gap-filler should settle. The Treaty of Fontainebleau page itself is silent on Etruria; the 27 October 1807 date and the annexation clause come from the Grand Duchy of Tuscany page. The two rows Cliopatria keeps for the Grand Duchy of Tuscany in 1800-1813 are 1,032 km2 fragments; the Grand Duchy of Tuscany dossier (another agent) should settle which land they are. Etruria's relation to France (a client kingdom) is not recorded as a vassal event because no page opened states it. Page budget: three pages opened (one empty).
